video.title: Loops: for, range and while
video.format_note: Animated explainer, 16:9, flat Darsi colours on paper-grey backgrounds. Code is typed out on a card, left to right in both languages. Narration in the lesson language; captions as separate files, never burned in.
cast: Ms Salma Haddad — the students’ maths teacher (main character)
Mr Joseph — the students’ computer studies teacher (cameo)
Narrator — the Darsi voice, talking to the student (warm, peer to peer)

scenes.narration: When I was at school, a punishment was writing a line a hundred times. My hand hurt for days! Python would do it in two lines, in less than a second.
Today: loops, and how to repeat without getting tired.
A for loop repeats the lines inside it. range of five gives five turns. The indented line runs once for each turn. Change five to a hundred, and it runs a hundred times.
The loop variable counts for you. range of one, six gives one, two, three, four and five: it stops just before six. Use it to print a countdown, a times table or numbered seats.
A loop can add up as it goes. Start total at zero. Each time round, add the next number. After the loop, total holds the answer: one plus two plus three plus four is ten.
A while loop repeats as long as its question is True. It’s perfect when you don’t know how many turns you’ll need, like a guessing game: keep asking until the guess is right.
Quick check! A loop says for i in range of three, and inside it, print Hello. How many times is Hello printed?
Three times. range of three starts at zero and stops before three: zero, one, two. Python often counts from zero, so get used to it!

Careful with while. If its question never becomes False, the loop never stops. Darsi stops your program after three seconds, so your phone won’t freeze. Then look for what should change inside the loop.
Loops can search, too. Checking one number after another is a for loop. A smarter way halves the range each time: guess the middle, then keep the half where the number must be. That’s a while loop.
In the app, open Guess the number. With one to a hundred, press only Try the middle: you never need more than seven guesses. Then race one by one against halving, up to a thousand.
Your turn. Total starts at zero, and a loop adds each number in range of one, four. What is the total at the end?
Six. Remember: for repeats once for each value in a range. range stops before its end, and often starts at zero. A total starts at zero before the loop. while repeats until its question is False.
Try it yourself: write a guess-the-number game with a while loop, and play it with a friend or someone at home. Count how many guesses they need, and teach them the halving trick!

checkpoints.prompt: for i in range(3), with print("Hello") inside. How many times is Hello printed?
checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — range(3) gives 0, 1 and 2: three turns.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — range(3) gives three values, 0, 1 and 2, so three Hellos.

checkpoints.prompt: total = 0; a loop adds each n in range(1, 4). What is total at the end?
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — range(1, 4) stops before 4, so it adds 1, 2 and 3: 6.
